For many years now, we’ve been using our data on 
UK companies to demonstrate London’s influence 
over the country’s high-growth scene. In 2021, the 
Capital remains a major force, but its dominance 
appears to be stabilising. 
In our first edition of this report, back in 2019, 
London accounted for 30% of high-growth UK 
companies. By our second edition, in May of 2020, 
that share had grown to 33%, and has remained 
steady since.  
And in terms of investment, London has been 
attracting a growing share of the pounds 
Foreword
invested into private UK companies over the past 
decade, but this growth has slowed in the past two 
years. In 2019, London-based companies attracted 
70p of every £1 invested in the UK, but this fell to 65p 
in 2020 and sits at 67p in Q1 2021. 
It's probably too soon to attribute this to the 
Government's ambition to 'level up' the regions, but 
it’s good to see that it’s not a lost cause. 
In this report, we map out the high-growth business 
landscape in London, from key sectors and funding 
trends to the impact of COVID-19.

We use eight criteria to identify 
high-growth and ambitious 
companies. Each of these is a sign 
that a business is either actively 
growing or creating ambitious 
growth plans. 
All companies featured in this report 
have met at least one of these 
growth triggers.

Accelerator attendance

Academic spinouts
What do we mean by ʻambitiousʼ?

There are currently 10,781 active, ambitious 
companies in London. Just 52% of businesses are 
in seed or venture stage, compared with 56% in 
May last year, showing a maturation of the market. 
An additional 970 have undergone an IPO or 
acquisition, and 2,445 are no longer trading. As 
expected during a global pandemic, companies 
are dying at a faster rate than they’re hitting 
high-growth milestones. The number of active 
companies has increased 15% in the last year, 
compared to a 24% increase in dead companies.
Stages of evolution
STAGES OF EVOLUTION OF HIGH-GROWTH LONDON BUSINESSES

66% of these companies (9,489) have grown 
through equity investment, by far the most popular 
method of financing growth in the City. In the last 12 
months, 827 companies in London have raised their 
first round of equity finance, representing 49% of 
first-round raisers in the UK.
Accelerators are also a very popular method of 
growth, but less so during the pandemic. Just 108 
London companies attended an accelerator 
programme in the last year, compared to 695 in the 
period prior. Despite its world-class universities, 
London has a low proportion of spinouts and grant 
recipients. 
NUMBER OF AMBITIOUS COMPANIES IN LONDON 
BY METHODS OF GROWTH
Methods of growth

London’s world-class fintech community is 
growing from strength to strength, with more 
than a thousand high-growth fintechs 
headquartered in the Capital, representing 
69% of all UK fintechs and 7% of London’s 
high-growth companies. 
Artificial intelligence is hot on its heels, with 
894 businesses. 
And despite declining investor interest in the 
sector, adtech is also a popular vertical in 
London.
NUMBER OF AMBITIOUS COMPANIES IN LONDON BY VERTICAL
Sectors and verticals

A staggering 2,658 companies operate from 
within Westminster’s eight square miles, and a 
further 1,679 in the City of London, neighbouring 
some of the corporate giants they hope to 
disrupt. 
It will be interesting to see if and how this 
landscape changes as more companies set up in 
a post-pandemic world. Physical presence has 
becomes less important over the course of the 
year, and remote-first setups have become more 
common. Early-stage startups, especially, may 
no longer deem central London oﬀice space, and 
the sky-high rent that comes with it, as essential.
DISTRIBUTION OF AMBITIOUS COMPANIES IN LONDON
Geographical distribution

Across the UK, Q1 2021 saw record levels of 
investment in terms of both volume and value 
of equity deals. London was no exception to 
this trend. In fact, London-based businesses 
drove this uptick in activity, with 285 rounds, 
worth £3.45b, secured during the first three 
months of the year. This represents 48% of all 
deals, up slightly from 46% in 2020, and 67% of 
all pounds invested, down from a high of 70% 
in 2019. 
The largest deals in the country are 
predominantly happening in the Capital, but 
regional companies are giving London a run for 
its money. 
Equity ﬁnance

LONDON-BASED COMPANIES 2011 - Q1 2021

OneWeb’s massive £941m funding round in March 
2019 gives Hammersmith and Fulham the largest 
average equity round size in the city (£4.32m). 
The company was acquired out of administration 
by the UK Government in November 2020. 
Westminster has the second-highest average 
(£2.91m) whilst Barking and Dagenham has the 
lowest at £178k. Just 19 fundraisings have taken 
place in the borough since 2011, the largest of 
which (£1.2m) was raised by indoor racing 
company Capital Karts in 2018.
AVERAGE FUNDING ROUND SIZE BY LOCAL AUTHORITY
Average round size

Since the start of the COVID-19 outbreak, 
London-based companies have been best placed 
to weather the storm, disproportionately 
operating in tech (and therefore more easily able 
to work from home) with agile, well-funded 
teams. But this inequality has levelled out across 
the year.
Now, 30% of ambitious London-based 
businesses are either potentially positively 
impacted by, or positively recovering from, the 
pandemic, compared to 27% across the rest of 
the country. For reference, those figures stood at 
45% and 53% in May 2020, respectively. 
Impact statuses
IMPACT OF COVID-19 ON HIGH-GROWTH LONDON BUSINESSES

Launched in May 2020, the Government’s 
Future Fund has supported equity-backed 
businesses to extend their runway during the 
pandemic. 
As of March 25th, a total of 1,236 convertible 
loan notes (CLN), worth £1.21b, have been 
approved. These have been allocated in 
keeping with the distribution of equity-backed 
companies across the country. London is 
home to 60% of the businesses eligible for the 
CLNs, and received 56% of Future Fund deals 
and 60% of pounds invested via the fund.
